churn_resistance.rationale: An upgrade would touch very few files: data behind one module, typed boundary, config in one place. What ages it is the untyped/validating-less seam to the upstream API and unchecked casts that the compiler is never asked to verify.

findings.issue: Upstream fetches have no timeout or abort signal; a stalled PokeAPI request hangs the SSR response and leaves a never-resolving promise cached, and no client-side timeout exists either.
findings.suggestion: Pass `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000)` to fetch and delete the cache entry on abort; the platform provides exactly this.

findings.issue: The entire PokeAPI response layer is `any` with regex-based URL/ID parsing (`pathOf`, `idOf`), so a shape change in the 'live service whose data can change at any moment' produces silent render-time failures rather than a caught error.
findings.suggestion: Type the parsed record at the `get()` boundary (or validate with a light Standard-Schema validator) so drift surfaces where the data enters, keeping the typed facade in types.ts.

findings.issue: `.validator((data: ListFilters) => data)` and `nameInput` are casts, not validation — the server-function input contract the framework provides is effectively disabled.
findings.suggestion: Use a real validator (zod/valibot/Standard Schema) or at least coerce and check the primitives, so future callers of these functions can't pass garbage.

findings.issue: `m._notFound` is not part of the documented RouteMatch type (docs expose `status: 'pending' | 'success' | 'error' | 'notFound'`); it relies on an underscore-prefixed internal field.
findings.suggestion: Check only `m.status === 'notFound'`, which is the documented and already-present condition.

findings.issue: The middleware only statically serves paths starting with `/assets/` and imports `./dist/server/server.js` by hand, coupling the server to Vite's current assets layout and Start's current output path.
findings.suggestion: Use a fall-through `staticMiddleware({ dir: clientDir })` for all paths (it falls through when no file matches), or the `srvx --prod -s dist/client dist/server/server.js` CLI the docs show, so renaming assetsDir or the entry path doesn't break `npm start`.

findings.issue: No `typecheck` script and `build` never runs `tsc --noEmit`, despite TypeScript 7 (the fast native compiler) already installed — the `_notFound` internal usage and `any` casts are never checked.
findings.suggestion: Add `"typecheck": "tsc --noEmit"` and wire it into `build` (the Start docs' own scripts do this); with TS7 it costs milliseconds.

findings.issue: Hand-rolled in-memory TTL cache (Map + Date.now + size-cap eviction + rejection cleanup) reimplements what the router and HTTP already offer.
findings.suggestion: At minimum keep it (it's small and justified for sub-fetches), but consider route-level `staleTime`/`loaderMaxAge` or HTTP cache headers on the server functions so the framework and any proxy share one caching story.

findings.issue: `cleanFilters` encodes the URL query contract inside the route component file and is re-implemented twice (validateSearch and navigate updaters), so adding a filter means editing one file in three places.
findings.suggestion: Move the filter normalization into lib/ (alongside ListFilters) so the query schema lives in one module.

summary: This app is written against TanStack Start's current stable generation, not a stale one: canonical `.validator()` server functions, the HeadContent/Scripts head API, Vite 8, React 19, TS 7, and a srvx production server matching the framework's own recipes. All upstream access sits behind one typed module, so a framework upgrade would touch almost nothing. What will age it is the seam to the PokeAPI itself — `any`-typed responses with cast validators and no fetch timeouts — which is exactly the boundary the spec says can change.
